newsitem.title: USA: Florida court hears lawyer open tobacco trial.
newsitem.headline: Florida court hears lawyer open tobacco trial.

text.p: Norwood "Woody" Wilner, the Florida lawyer who last year won the largest-ever judgment against the tobacco industry, launched a lawsuit against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co on Wednesday by saying cigarette makers failed to use reasonable care in promoting and selling their products.

In a courtroom packed with lawyers, journalists and members of the public, Wilner opened the trial by outlining a medical history of cigarettes, saying that scientists had drawn links between smoking and lung cancer as early as the 1920s and that tobacco companies knew it.

"Lung cancer has essentially one cause, and that's smoking," Wilner told the six-member jury hearing the wrongful death lawsuit known as Raulerson vs. R.J. Reynolds. Reynolds is a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.
Plaintiff Dana Raulerson, who sued the tobacco company on behalf of the estate of her late sister Jean Connor, was in the courtroom as opening statements were made.

The crowd was so large for the trial's opening that the proceedings were carried by closed-circuit televisions to two other rooms in the Jacksonville courthouse, where media and members of the public were accommodated.
Wilner told jurors that cigarette smoking caused mutations in DNA -- human molecules that carry genetic information -- and said 90 percent of lung cancers were attributable to active smoking.
He told jurors that tobacco companies had failed to use "reasonable care" in promoting and distributing their products and said warnings on cigarette packages were inadequate.
During his 65-minute opening statement, Wilner showed jurors pictures of Connor, a bank manager and mother of three, before and after she was diagnosed with lung cancer. She died in 1995 at age 49.
Two of her sons were in the courtroom, as were lawyers for Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp.

Last summer, a Jacksonville jury rendered a landmark $750,000 judgment against Brown & Williamson, a unit of B.A.T Industries Plc. The judgment, which is being appealed, was the largest to date against a tobacco company.
The jury, four women and two men, was seated earlier Wednesday.
